mcqs.question: According to Alan Kay's original framing, what makes `shape.area()` conceptually different from `calculateArea(shape)`?
options: It is a message sent to `shape`, which decides for itself how to respond, rather than a fixed function receiving `shape` as an argument
It runs faster because method calls skip the function call stack
It is only different in syntax — both are resolved identically at compile time
It requires `shape` to be declared with the `private` keyword
mcqs.explanation: Kay's core idea was message passing: the receiving object decides how to respond, which is what enables dynamic dispatch. It is not a performance claim or a syntax-only difference — the resolution mechanism (compile-time fixed vs runtime lookup) is genuinely different, and private has nothing to do with it.

mcqs.question: What is the key mechanical difference between `calculateArea(shape)` in imperative code and `shape.area()` in OOP code?
options: The imperative call site is bound to fixed code at compile time; the OOP call resolves to different code depending on `shape`'s runtime type
The OOP call always executes slower due to extra indirection with no other difference
The imperative version cannot accept different shape types at all
There is no real difference — both ultimately call the same machine instructions
mcqs.explanation: The call-site-vs-runtime-type distinction is exactly what dynamic dispatch buys: the same source line routes to different code depending on the receiver's type, unlike a statically bound function call. The imperative version can accept different shapes just fine — it just has to branch on type explicitly inside one function.

mcqs.question: You add a new `Triangle` class with its own `area()` method to a codebase that already has code calling `shape.area()` on a list of shapes. What has to change in that existing calling code for `Triangle` to work correctly?
options: The calling code needs an added `elif isinstance(shape, Triangle)` branch
Nothing — dynamic dispatch routes the call to `Triangle.area()` automatically once a `Triangle` instance flows through it
The `total_area` function's signature must be updated to accept `Triangle` explicitly
The dispatch table for every existing shape class must be regenerated
mcqs.explanation: Dynamic dispatch is precisely the mechanism that avoids type-checking branches at call sites — the object supplies its own table entry, so existing calling code needs zero changes. That's the paradigm's central promise: extend by adding a type, not by editing shared code.

mcqs.question: In JavaScript's prototype-based object model, what happens when you call `obj.method()` and `method` isn't defined directly on `obj`?
options: The call fails immediately with a compile-time error
JavaScript silently falls back to calling `toString()` instead
The runtime walks up `obj`'s prototype chain looking for `method` on a linked prototype object
JavaScript creates a new class on the fly to satisfy the call
mcqs.explanation: Prototype-based inheritance works by delegation: a lookup miss on the object itself walks the prototype chain until the method is found or the chain ends. JavaScript has no compile-time type checking to fail at, and it does not fabricate classes or fall back to unrelated methods.

mcqs.question: Why did "favor composition over inheritance" become conventional wisdom for handling cases like a `RubberDuck` that shouldn't inherit `fly()` from `Duck`?
options: Because inheritance is always slower at runtime than composition
Because composition lets you assign or swap a behavior per instance (e.g. a `NoFlight` behavior) without restructuring the class hierarchy or coupling to ancestor implementation details
Because most languages no longer support multiple inheritance
Because composition removes the need for dynamic dispatch entirely
mcqs.explanation: Composition avoids the implementation coupling and hierarchy-editing problems of deep inheritance by delegating to a swappable behavior object per instance. It isn't a runtime-speed argument, has nothing to do with multiple-inheritance support, and composition still relies on dynamic dispatch through the delegated interface.
